Front: What are the three parts of a stream pipeline, and when does it actually run?
Back: Source (e.g. payments.stream()), zero or more intermediate operations (filter, map, sorted, limit), and one terminal operation (toList, forEach, count). Intermediate operations are lazy: nothing runs until the terminal operation is called.

Front: filter() vs map(): what does each do and which functional interface does it take?
Back: filter(Predicate<T>) selects: true keeps the element, false drops it. map(Function<T,R>) transforms each element, e.g. map(Payment::getAmount) turns Stream<Payment> into Stream<BigDecimal>. forEach takes a Consumer<T>.

Front: Why is `.filter(isValid).limit(2)` different from `.limit(2).filter(isValid)`, and why can the first stop early?
Back: Order matters: the first finds valid payments and takes two; the second takes the first two payments and then filters them. Because streams are lazy and limit() short-circuits, the first pipeline can stop as soon as two matches are found without reading the whole source.

Front: How should you check `payment.getMethod()` is PIX, and why not compareTo()?
Back: Use `p.getMethod() == PaymentMethod.PIX`. Enum constants are singletons, so == is correct and null-safe (null → false). compareTo() compares declaration order (ordinal), not equality, and throws NullPointerException if getMethod() is null.

Front: In GET /payments/type/{method}, what do @RestController and @PathVariable do, and what happens with /payments/type/pix?
Back: @RestController (= @Controller + @ResponseBody) writes return values to the response body; Jackson turns List<Payment> into JSON. @PathVariable binds {method} and Spring converts "PIX" to PaymentMethod.PIX. Conversion is case-sensitive, so "pix" fails and Spring returns 400 Bad Request.
